subject: Hybrid streaming vs sync SLA — time-to-first-token and sustained token/sec for FinTru pilot
messages:
From: FinTru SRE Lead <sre.lead@fintru.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTru Procurement <procurement@fintru.io>
Date: 2028-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on streaming vs sync SLA for pilot

Logan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to follow up with a few technical clarifications before we sign the pilot MOU. Attached are a short list of SLA questions and our expected traffic profile (fintru_pilot_traffic_profile.xlsx). Key items we need answers for:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming endpoints vs sync (per-request) endpoints for models in the 2–13B range. We have a latency-sensitive ingestion pipeline that needs predictable first-token bounds.
- Sustained token/sec guarantees per connection (we plan many long-lived streaming connections from our ingestion cluster).
- Fallback behavior: if streaming emission drops below threshold, does Redwood automatically fall back to a sync path? What does the customer see during fallback?
- Warmup/priming: you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching. Is there an expected warmup window that would affect TTFT guarantees?
- Any carveouts you anticipate during pilot (e.g., prewarm period, model-variant-specific thresholds).

Would appreciate a written proposal we can circulate internally to SRE and procurement. Our preference is to have clear numeric commitments we can reference in the MOU (p95/p99 where possible) and an operational runbook for escalations.

Regards,
Maya Singh
SRE Lead, FinTru Financial
Attachments: fintru_initial_sla_questions.pdf, fintru_pilot_traffic_profile.xlsx
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarification on streaming vs sync SLA for pilot

Team —

FYI: FinTru sent a concise list of asks around TTFT and sustained tokens for their ingestion pilot. They want hard numbers for the MOU. I sketched a proposal below; please review for technical accuracy and flag anything that would be a blocker for Dedicated or Private pilots.

Proposal (high level):
- Streaming TTFT (p95): 300ms for sequences < 512 tokens when routed to a dedicated pool with prewarmed KV cache.
- Streaming TTFT during initial 30-day pilot warmup (p95): 450ms — we call this the "prewarm window" and document it in the MOU.
- Sustained tokens/sec per streaming connection (guarantee): 180 tokens/sec sustained, with short bursts to 500 tokens/sec for <= 30s when pool capacity permits.
- Fallback behavior: if a streaming connection's emission rate drops under the sustained bound for >15s due to scheduling, we failover to a sync endpoint with best-effort token delivery and prioritized retry semantics. We provide transparent diagnostics (trace id, fallback reason).
- Operational controls: explicit prewarm API for FinTru to request KV prime; telemetry export (token emission curve, TTFT distribution) to their SRE project in the Console.

Constraints & questions for red-teaming:
- Are we comfortable contractually committing to 300ms p95 outside of Dedicated reserved capacity?
- Do we need to limit model variants in the MOU (e.g., quantized 8-bit only) to make these numbers reliable?

If this looks reasonable I'll draft a short external note to FinTru.

— Logan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-29T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification on streaming vs sync SLA for pilot

Logan —

Quick technical notes and suggested wording for the MOU. TL;DR: we can meet the numbers with caveats; spell them out.

Notes:
- TTFT variability comes from three sources: model compile/runtime kernel choice, KV cache miss for long context priming, and scheduling contention on multi-tenant GPUs.
- For reliable 300ms p95 we should require either (a) dedicated prewarmed lanes (Dedicated pool) or (b) explicit prewarm API calls that run < 30s of priming tokens before traffic.
- Quantization matters: q4/q8 models will have faster kernel paths. If FinTru wants fp16 variants the TTFT band could widen by ~20–40% on current infra.
- Sustained tokens/sec per connection is a function of token size and attention window; recommend we tie the guarantee to a traffic profile (their attached spreadsheet).

Suggested contractual language: "For the agreed pilot models and traffic profile, Redwood will commit to a streaming time-to-first-token (TTFT) of 350–450ms p95 during the initial 30-day warmup period and 300–350ms p95 thereafter when traffic is routed to the agreed Dedicated pool or after successful prewarm operations. Sustained per-connection throughput is guaranteed at 150–200 tokens/second with burst capacity up to 450–500 tokens/second for up to 30 seconds, subject to overall pool capacity. All guarantees assume the customer adheres to the accepted traffic profile and uses supported model variants (quantized or otherwise mutually agreed)."

Operational escalation: include an SRE contact path and an automatic capacity-reservation workflow (in Console) for emergency scaling.

If we accept the 450ms pilot p95 ceiling, I'm okay. Recommend we include explicit exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force-major (as usual).

— Karthik
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <sre.lead@fintru.io>, FinTru Procurement <procurement@fintru.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-29T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on streaming vs sync SLA for pilot — proposed commitments

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. After discussing with our runtime team I've put together a concise proposal we can include in the pilot MOU. Attached is a short APS (pilot acceptance) spreadsheet that maps your traffic profile to the commitments below.

Proposal (pilot MOU language, summary):
- Streaming TTFT (p95): 450ms during the initial 30-day pilot warmup window; 350ms p95 after successful prewarm or after the warmup window.
- Sustained per-connection throughput: guaranteed 180 tokens/sec sustained, with burst capacity up to 500 tokens/sec for windows up to 30 seconds, subject to pool capacity.
- Fallback behavior: Redwood will automatically route requests to the sync endpoint with documented retry semantics when streaming emission falls below agreed thresholds for >15 seconds. Customers will receive trace ids and a fallback code in telemetry.
- Prewarm API: FinTru may invoke a documented prewarm operation prior to production cutover; Redwood will coordinate a one-time priming run to populate KV caches for the pilot models.
- Operational support: on-call SRE escalation path, weekly telemetry export to FinTru's Console project, and shared runbook entry in the drive link below.

Next steps: confirm that these numbers are acceptable to SRE and Procurement and we will convert into a short MOU addendum. If FinTru needs firmer p95 numbers earlier, we can discuss Dedicated capacity pricing to guarantee 300ms p95 from day one.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
